what: A lie told to someone who loves you.

excerpts.text:
HELMER. Yes. Has anyone been here?
NORA. Here? No.
HELMER. That is strange. I saw Krogstad going out of the gate.
NORA. Did you? Oh yes, I forgot, Krogstad was here for a moment.
HELMER. Nora, I can see from your manner that he has been here begging you to say a good word for him.
NORA. Yes.
HELMER. And you were to appear to do it of your own accord; you were to conceal from me the fact of his having been here; didn’t he beg that of you too?

moves.move: She repeats the word to buy a second, then lies in one syllable. Liars keep it short.

moves.at: That is strange. I saw Krogstad going out of the gate.
moves.move: He knows already. The lie is tested with mild interest, which is worse than anger.

moves.at: Did you? Oh yes, I forgot
moves.move: A lie mended with a smaller lie, and the tone stays light. The player holds what she is hiding, so the lightness hurts.

moves.at: I can see from your manner
moves.move: He reads her wrongly and kindly. Someone who loves you explains away your lie for you.
She accepts his wrong explanation, because it is safer than the truth. The lie gets easier because he helps.

excerpts.text:
She was sitting at the table and smiled at him.
“Do you feel better?” he asked.
“I feel fine,” she said. “There’s nothing wrong with me. I feel fine.”

moves.move: The lie starts as a piece of staging, before any word.
A loving question that wants only one answer. He is asking to be let off.
Plain words, nothing to catch hold of. It works because of what the scene already planted.

moves.at: There’s nothing wrong with me. I feel fine.”
moves.move: She says it again, unasked. The repeat is the only sign. No closing quip; the scene stops there.

excerpts.text:
OTHELLO. Is’t lost? is’t gone? speak, is it out of the way?
DESDEMONA. Heaven bless us!
OTHELLO. Say you?
DESDEMONA. It is not lost, but what and if it were?
OTHELLO. How?
DESDEMONA. I say it is not lost.
OTHELLO. Fetch’t, let me see ’t.
DESDEMONA. Why, so I can, sir, but I will not now. This is a trick to put me from my suit. Pray you, let Cassio be receiv’d again.
OTHELLO. Fetch me the handkerchief! My mind misgives.
DESDEMONA. Come, come. You’ll never meet a more sufficient man.
OTHELLO. The handkerchief!
DESDEMONA. I pray, talk me of Cassio.

moves.move: An exclamation in place of an answer.

moves.at: It is not lost, but what and if it were?
moves.move: A denial and a dare in one line. Half of it already gives her away.

moves.at: I say it is not lost.
moves.move: Firmer the second time, which is how a lie sounds when pressed.
She can't produce the thing, so she makes not producing it a matter of will.

moves.at: This is a trick to put me from my suit.
moves.move: She accuses him and changes the subject to what she came to ask. Attack is the cover.

moves.at: I pray, talk me of Cassio.
moves.move: Each is now on their own track, one thing repeated against another.
